title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 302
paragraphs: Thus they deal with the corpses that are prepared in the most costly way. But for those who desire the middle way and wish to avoid great cost, they prepare the corpse as follows. Having filled their syringes with the oil that is obtained from cedar-wood, with this they immediately fill the belly of the corpse — and they do this without having cut it open or taken out the bowels, injecting the oil by the anus, and having stopped the drench from running back they keep the corpse the appointed number of days for embalming. On the last of the days they let the cedar oil come out from the belly, which they before put in; and it has such power that it brings out with it the bowels and the interior organs of the body all dissolved; and the natron dissolves the flesh, so that there is left of the corpse only the skin and the bones. When they have done this they give back the corpse at once in that condition, without working upon it any more.
